summary.value: The Iowa Blue is a rare American dual-purpose chicken that first turned up near Decorah, Iowa, in the early 1900s. Its true origin is unknown, and the local story that a pheasant fathered the first chicks cannot be true, since pheasants and chickens do not interbreed. Despite the name, the birds are not blue: they have a silvery white head and a dark body with white penciling, plus a single comb and red earlobes. Roosters weigh about 7 pounds and hens about 6. Hens lay a fair number of brown eggs and often go broody and raise chicks well. The birds are fairly docile, though some are a bit skittish, and they forage well on free range. Roosters are known as bold guards against hawks. The breed nearly died out after Iowa hatcheries dropped it and has never been accepted into a show standard, so it suits homesteaders who want a working bird.
